findings.problem: LedgerWorkflow has no typestate enum; lifecycle is untracked by the type system
findings.failure_mode: any sequence of boolean transitions is representable including validated->unsent, sent->validated, or double-sent; the compiler cannot enforce valid state transitions
findings.fix: introduce a `LedgerStatus` enum (e.g., Pending, Validated, Sent) as a field or the struct itself; replace `status`, `is_validated`, `is_sent`, `sent_at_epoch_ms` with a single enum field whose variants own their data

findings.problem: status is a String allowing arbitrary values ("sent", "foo", "", null-like strings) instead of a closed enum
findings.failure_mode: callers can set status to any string including invalid values like "snt", "SENT", or "", and comparison logic would silently accept garbage instead of failing at compile time
findings.fix: replace `pub status: String` with `pub status: LedgerStatus` where `LedgerStatus` is an enum with exactly the valid domain states (Pending, Validated, Sent)

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are independent booleans that cannot express mutually exclusive or ordered lifecycle states
findings.failure_mode: both booleans can be true simultaneously (double-sent), both false while status says "sent" (inconsistent), or true in impossible combinations like validated=false but sent=true
findings.fix: replace both booleans with a single `LedgerStatus` enum variant; embed `sent_at_epoch_ms: u64` as data on the Sent variant so lifecycle data lives in the variant that owns it

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is a separate field from is_sent, so the Option can be None while is_sent is true (or vice versa), creating inconsistent state
findings.failure_mode: caller sets is_sent=true and sent_at_epoch_ms=None, producing a ledger that claims sent but has no timestamp; this is a silent data integrity violation indistinguishable from a bug
findings.fix: move `sent_at_epoch_ms` into the `Sent` variant of a `LedgerStatus` enum so the timestamp is required when and only when the ledger is in the sent state

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive with no domain validation; any string is a valid ledger ID
findings.failure_mode: empty strings, whitespace, duplicate IDs, or malformed identifiers are accepted as valid ledger IDs; no constraint enforcement at the type level
findings.fix: replace with `pub id: LedgerId` where `LedgerId` is a newtype wrapping a validated string (e.g., `struct LedgerId(String)` or `struct LedgerId([u8; N])`) with a fallible smart constructor

findings.problem: raw String and bool primitives cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors; callers can construct LedgerWorkflow directly with invalid status strings and inconsistent booleans
findings.failure_mode: no constructor enforces domain invariants, so any caller bypasses the parse boundary and creates invalid domain states directly
findings.fix: add a `LedgerWorkflow::new(id: LedgerId, status: LedgerStatus) -> Result<Self, LedgerError>` smart constructor that accepts only validated domain types; remove all public fields behind `pub(crate)` or private accessors

findings.problem: mark_sent blindly overwrites status and sets is_sent=true regardless of the current state; no transition guard
findings.failure_mode: calling mark_sent on an already-sent ledger produces double-sent; calling it on a validated ledger skips the validated state entirely; no invariant checking at the function boundary
findings.fix: replace with a method on a typestate-aware enum that enforces valid transitions, e.g. `impl LedgerWorkflow { fn mark_sent(self) -> Result<Self, TransitionError> }` returning an error if not in a sendable state

findings.problem: no benchmark, profiler, allocation analysis, or second-ring evidence exists for mark_sent or LedgerWorkflow
findings.failure_mode: performance characteristics of the to_string() allocation on every mark_sent call are unmeasured; under Holzman, performance claims require workload, target, baseline, and evidence
findings.fix: add a criterion or custom benchmark for mark_sent measuring allocation count, allocation size, and throughput; add a #[bench] or criterion harness and report baseline vs new numbers with variance

findings.problem: no test targets, no benchmark targets, and no CI gate defined in Cargo.toml; the canonical verification gate cannot be run
findings.failure_mode: no evidence that cargo fmt, clippy, or tests pass; Holzman requires canonical gate evidence before delivery
findings.fix: add [[test]] and [[bench]] sections to Cargo.toml, create tests/, and run cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --lib -- -D warnings, and cargo test

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent allocation and throughput
no profiler data for hot path analysis
no allocation analysis (no try_reserve, no bounded allocation evidence)
no second-ring evidence (no measured command output, no cargo clippy test, no cargo test output)
no command-truth evidence that verification gates ran
residual_risk: The LedgerWorkflow type permits all illegal state combinations at compile time: any status string value, any boolean combination of is_validated/is_sent, and inconsistent sent_at_epoch_ms. The mark_sent function has no transition guards. No benchmarks, profilers, or verification gates have evidence. This is a structural typestate violation that cannot be patched; the type system must be restructured to make illegal states unrepresentable. Without a typestate enum, all consumer code inherits the same invalid-state risk.
